headline: The Select Board set Town Meeting dates, funded Route 9 wastewater planning, and denied an Open Space appointment, while schools advanced Neary planning.
synopsis: The Select Board scheduled the Fall Special Town Meeting for October 17, 2026, and the 2027 Annual Town Meeting for March 20, 2027. It also approved $30,000 for financial analysis of a Route 9 wastewater district, stripped a $105,000 drone request from police year-end spending, and voted against reappointing Freddie Gillespie to the Open Space Preservation Commission. In school developments, the Elementary School Building Committee launched a revised Neary School study with Tappé Architects focused on tiered renovation choices, while the School Committee approved a three-year contract for support staff. Additionally, the Personnel Board adopted FY27 municipal wage rates and finalized a contract for a comprehensive salary study.

highlights.title: Town Meeting dates set for fall and spring
highlights.why: The Select Board scheduled the Fall Special Town Meeting for Saturday, October 17, 2026, and the Annual Town Meeting for Saturday, March 20, 2027. Both sessions will start at 10:00 AM on Saturdays to accommodate families and seniors.

highlights.title: Funding approved for Route 9 wastewater study
highlights.why: The Select Board voted 4-1 to allocate $30,000 from Economic Development Committee surplus funds for MassDevelopment consultant projections. The analysis will model property tax revenues to support a proposed District Improvement Financing article in the fall.

highlights.title: Neary School study relaunches with tiered options
highlights.why: Tappé Architects met with the Elementary School Building Committee to develop multiple renovation tiers ranging from basic code repairs to educational upgrades. The architects suggested October is too early for a full construction funding vote.

highlights.title: Select Board blocks $105,000 police drone program
highlights.why: While approving year-end surplus funds for medical gear and ballistic plates, the board excluded a $105,000 five-year drone request, stating it should be vetted by the Capital Committee and Town Meeting.

highlights.title: Freddie Gillespie denied Open Space reappointment
highlights.why: The Select Board voted 0-5 against reappointing longtime conservation volunteer Freddie Gillespie to the Open Space Preservation Commission, citing past procedural disputes and committee restructuring goals.

highlights.title: Three-year contract approved for school support personnel
highlights.why: The School Committee unanimously approved a three-year collective bargaining agreement with the Southborough Teachers Association covering Unit C administrative assistants and educational support professionals.
